title: livekit
same: Every counted sample's results were read from its own job logs. In all 15 counted samples (5 per configuration) the same 1,700 checks ran and passed: 1,690 Go test results from the Test job (packages, tests and subtests), golangci-lint, the mage build, and for each of the two images (server and test-server) the Go binary and the image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The same 25 Go entries were reported as skipped in every sample. The images were not compared byte for byte: with the fix, the Go binaries for arm64 are cross-compiled on the x64 runner instead of compiled under emulation, so the checks above, not a byte comparison, are the evidence that the builds are equivalent.
notes: **Lane: merges to the default branch.** This page measures merges to livekit's default branch, `master`: each sample replays the merge of `401ddb14`. PR updates were not measured, because the agent PR changes the two Docker release builds, and upstream runs those only on merges to the default branch (and on version tags), never on a pull request.

**Workflows in this merge.** The replayed merge changes `pkg/rtc/participant.go` and `pkg/rtc/participant_internal_test.go`, and three workflows run: Test (`buildtest.yaml`), Release to Docker (`docker.yaml`, the server image) and Release Test Server to Docker (`test-server-docker.yaml`). Both Docker workflows build their image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. `release.yaml` runs only on version tags and `slack-notifier.yaml` only on pull-request events, so neither is part of these numbers.

**Bench-only changes, identical in every configuration (GitHub, StarSling unchanged, StarSling + agent PR) and never part of the agent PR:**
  - Switched off: the Docker Hub login and publishing of the images in both Docker workflows (both images are still built for both CPUs, then discarded). The Docker Hub secrets do not exist here, and nothing may be published. Upstream's own runs include publishing the images.
  - Secret references for the Docker Hub secrets are removed; they were already empty in every configuration.
  - One subtest, `TestTurnRelay/allow`, is skipped in every setup: it hard-codes `10.0.0.0/8` and `192.168.0.0/16` as the allowed relay ranges, and StarSling's runners use `172.20.0.0/16`, so it fails there and passes on GitHub. The parent `TestTurnRelay` and its other subtests still run.
  - On the agent PR's branch only, never in a replay: the `slack-notifier` job is limited to the upstream repository, so reviewing or merging the agent PR does not start a Slack job that has no secrets here. The agent PR's own CI had one failure, that same `TestTurnRelay/allow` subtest (the PR's CI does not skip it); a comment on the PR explains it.

**One voided sample, replaced.** Round 1's StarSling-unchanged sample in experiment `full-1` ([run](https://github.com/starsling-demo-org/benchmark-livekit/actions/runs/43950160108)) was voided: it ran while StarSling runners in this organization used disk storage instead of their usual RAM disk, and this benchmark counts StarSling samples only with the RAM disk. It was re-run once, in experiment `full-1-x1` ([run](https://github.com/starsling-demo-org/benchmark-livekit/actions/runs/43992505388)), and that run fills round 1. The voided run is in no median; with it, the StarSling-unchanged median wait would be 456 s instead of 455 s, and the median runner time is the same (16.80 min). The record this page is generated from, `full-1-with-x1`, is `full-1` with the voided sample kept but not counted, and the `full-1-x1` run filed as that slot's replacement (`…-rep1-starsling-baseline-retry1`); `bench verify` re-checked all 15 counted samples on it.

**Runner sizes.** Upstream's `ubuntu-latest` jobs run on GitHub `ubuntu-26.04-4core` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB) and StarSling `starsling-ubuntu-26.04` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB). StarSling's 4 vCPU runners can burst to 5 vCPU and 32 GB RAM (Afterburner); GitHub's 4-core runners have 16 GB. Every job in this merge runs on those labels.

**Upstream reference (context only; not like-for-like; not the headline).** What upstream sees today: a median 22.0 min per merge to the default branch on upstream's own GitHub runners (n=10, most recent comparable merges within the last 60 days; standard runners, warm caches, many commits; not a like-for-like replay).

agentPrs.summary: Run the Go builder stage of `Dockerfile` and `cmd/test-server/Dockerfile` on the runner's own CPU (`FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM`), so Go cross-compiles the arm64 binary instead of compiling it under CPU emulation. Three one-line changes, including `.github/scripts/go-version.sh`, which still reads the Go version (1.27.3) from the new `FROM` line.

whatWasSlow: Every merge to livekit's default branch runs three workflows side by side: Test, and two Docker release builds, the server image and the test-server image, each built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The arm64 images were built under a CPU emulator (QEMU) on the x64 runner, so their whole Go compile ran at emulation speed. The server image build is the longest job: in this benchmark it took a median 966 s of the 968 s merge on GitHub, and 444 s of the 455 s merge on StarSling runners before any change. Cold, with no caches.
whatWeChanged:
The original showcase for this project proposed one fix: build the Go stage of both Dockerfiles on the runner's own CPU and cross-compile for arm64, instead of emulating it. We measured it on StarSling, cold, with 5 runs on each side (the CI as it was, and the CI with the fix), on the step it changes.

| Fix | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Run the Go builder stage of `Dockerfile` and `cmd/test-server/Dockerfile` on the runner's own CPU and cross-compile for arm64, instead of emulating it | `Build and push` steps of both Docker jobs: 581 s to 118 s (median), **4.9x faster**; every run with the fix beat every run without it | Kept (agent PR 1) |

On the whole wait the gain is smaller, 1.3x (455 s to 356 s): the Test job (median 346 s with the fix) runs alongside the Docker builds and is now the longest job. The fix uses no cache, so the full benchmark runs cold only. It compares GitHub-hosted runners, StarSling with the CI unchanged, and StarSling with the agent PR applied, over 5 rounds.
